At \(x=1\), the expression inside the bracket is \(-\dfrac{4}{3}+10-16=-\dfrac{22}{3}\).

[JEE Main 2024, 31 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let the centroid, circumcentre, and orthocentre be \(G=A(a,b)\), \(O=B(3,4)\), and \(H=C(-6,-8)\), respectively.

To obtain the relation among these three points, take the circumcentre \(O\) as the temporary origin.

Let the position vectors of the three vertices of the triangle be \(\vec{u}\), \(\vec{v}\), and \(\vec{w}\).

Since \(O\) is the circumcentre, \(|\vec{u}|=|\vec{v}|=|\vec{w}|\).

The point with position vector \(\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}\) lies on the altitude through the vertex \(\vec{u}\), because \((\vec{v}+\vec{w})\cdot(\vec{v}-\vec{w})=|\vec{v}|^2-|\vec{w}|^2=0\).

The same argument applies to the other two altitudes, so \(\overrightarrow{OH}=\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}\).

The centroid satisfies \(\overrightarrow{OG}=\dfrac{\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}}{3}\).

Therefore, \(\overrightarrow{OH}=3\overrightarrow{OG}\).

In coordinate form, \(H-O=3(G-O)\), so \(H=3G-2O\).

Substituting the given coordinates gives \((-6,-8)=3(a,b)-2(3,4)\).

Therefore, \((-6,-8)=(3a-6,3b-8)\).

Comparing the coordinates gives \(a=0\) and \(b=0\).

Hence \(P(2a+3,7b+5)=(3,5)\).

A direction vector parallel to the line \(x-2y-1=0\) is \((2,1)\).

Therefore, the line through \(P(3,5)\) parallel to it can be written as \(x=3+2t\) and \(y=5+t\).

At the point where this line meets \(2x+3y-4=0\), we have \(2(3+2t)+3(5+t)-4=0\).

Thus \(6+4t+15+3t-4=0\).

Hence \(17+7t=0\), so \(t=-\dfrac{17}{7}\).

The distance travelled along the direction vector \((2,1)\) is \(|t|\sqrt{2^2+1^2}\).

Therefore, the required distance is \(\dfrac{17}{7}\sqrt{5}=\dfrac{17\sqrt{5}}{7}\).

Hence the correct option is \(\mathrm{C}\).

questions.question:
Let \(a, b, c\) be the lengths of three sides of a triangle satisfying the condition a2+b2x2-2b(a+c)x+b2+c2=0. If the set of all possible values of \(x\) is the interval (α,β), then 12α2+β2 is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 31 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
\((a^2+b^2)x^2-2b(a+c)x+(b^2+c^2)=0\).

For real roots, its discriminant must be non-negative.

Thus \(\left[-2b(a+c)\right]^2-4(a^2+b^2)(b^2+c^2)\geq0\).

\(b^2(a+c)^2-(a^2+b^2)(b^2+c^2)\geq0\).

On expanding,

\(b^2(a^2+2ac+c^2)-(a^2b^2+a^2c^2+b^4+b^2c^2)\geq0\).

This simplifies to

\(2ab^2c-a^2c^2-b^4\geq0\),

that is, \(-(ac-b^2)^2\geq0\).

A negative square can be non-negative only when it is zero.

Hence \(ac=b^2\).

Let \(a=t^2c\)

and \(b=tc\),

where \(t>0\).

The repeated root of the quadratic is

\(x=\dfrac{b(a+c)}{a^2+b^2}\).

Substituting \(a=t^2c\) and \(b=tc\),

\(x=\dfrac{tc(t^2c+c)}{t^4c^2+t^2c^2}\)

\(=\dfrac{t(t^2+1)}{t^2(t^2+1)}\)

\(=\dfrac1t\).

Since \(a,b,c\) are sides of a triangle,

\(a+b>c\) and \(b+c>a\).

These give \(t^2+t>1\) and \(t+1>t^2\).

The first inequality gives

\(t>\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\).

The second gives

\(t<\dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\).

Therefore, \(\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}<t<\dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\).

Since \(x=\dfrac1t\), the possible values of \(x\) form the same interval:

\(\alpha=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\),

\(\beta=\dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\).

Now \(\alpha+\beta=\sqrt5\)

and \(\alpha\beta=1\).

Hence \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=5-2=3\).

Therefore, \(12(\alpha^2+\beta^2)=12\cdot3=36\).

Let the coefficient of xr in the expansion of (x+3)n-1+(x+3)n-2(x+2)+(x+3)n-3(x+2)2+…+(x+2)n-1 be αr. If ∑r=0nαr=βn-γn,β,γ∈ℕ, then the value of β2+γ2 equals

this equals \(\dfrac{(x+3)^n-(x+2)^n}{(x+3)-(x+2)}\)

questions.question:
120π3∫0πx2sinxcosxsin4x+cos4xdx  is equal to _____________.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 31 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(I=\int_0^\pi \frac{x^2\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}dx\).

Put \(h(x)=\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}\).

Then \(I=\int_0^\pi x^2h(x)dx\).

Using the property \(\int_0^{2a}F(x)dx=\int_0^a\{F(x)+F(2a-x)\}dx\),

we get \(I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\{x^2h(x)+(\pi-x)^2h(\pi-x)\}dx\).

Now \(h(\pi-x)=\frac{\sin(\pi-x)\cos(\pi-x)}{\sin^4(\pi-x)+\cos^4(\pi-x)}=-\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}=-h(x)\).

Therefore \(I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\{x^2h(x)-(\pi-x)^2h(x)\}dx\).

So \(I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\{x^2-(\pi-x)^2\}h(x)dx\).

Thus \(I=\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}(2x-\pi)h(x)dx\)...\((1)\)

Again applying the property in \((1)\) on \(\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\),

\(I=\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\left[2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)-\pi\right]h\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)dx\).

Now \(h\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=h(x)\).

Therefore \(I=\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}(-2x)h(x)dx\)...\((2)\)

Adding \((1)\) and \((2)\),

\(2I=\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\{(2x-\pi)-2x\}h(x)dx\).

So \(2I=-\pi^2\int_0^{\pi/2}h(x)dx\).

Therefore \(I=-\frac{\pi^2}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}dx\).

Let \(J=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}dx\).

Dividing numerator and denominator by \(\cos^4x\),

\(J=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\tan x\sec^2x}{\tan^4x+1}dx\).

Put \(t=\tan x\), so \(dt=\sec^2x\,dx\).

When \(x=0\), \(t=0\), and when \(x\to\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(t\to\infty\).

Thus \(J=\int_0^\infty\frac{t}{t^4+1}dt\).

Put \(u=t^2\), so \(du=2t\,dt\).

Therefore \(J=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^\infty\frac{du}{u^2+1}\).

So \(J=\frac{1}{2}\left[\tan^{-1}u\right]_0^\infty=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{4}\).

Hence \(I=-\frac{\pi^2}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{4}=-\frac{\pi^3}{8}\).

Now \(\left|\frac{120}{\pi^3}I\right|=\left|\frac{120}{\pi^3}\cdot\left(-\frac{\pi^3}{8}\right)\right|\).

Therefore \(\left|\frac{120}{\pi^3}I\right|=15\).

questions.question:
Let A(-2,-1),B(1,0),C(α,β) and D(γ,δ) be the vertices of a parallelogram \(ABCD\). If the point \(C\) lies on \(2x - y = 5\) and the point \(D\) lies on \(3x - 2y = 6\), then the value of |α+β+γ+δ| is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 31 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For parallelogram \(ABCD\), the diagonals bisect each other.

Therefore, \(A+C=B+D\).

Hence \(C=B+D-A\).

Using \(A(-2,-1)\), \(B(1,0)\), and \(D(\gamma,\delta)\), we get \(C(\gamma+3,\delta+1)\).

Therefore, \(\alpha=\gamma+3\) and \(\beta=\delta+1\).

Since \(C\) lies on \(2x-y=5\), we get \(2(\gamma+3)-(\delta+1)=5\).

Hence \(2\gamma-\delta=0\).

Since \(D\) lies on \(3x-2y=6\), we have \(3\gamma-2\delta=6\).

From \(2\gamma-\delta=0\), we get \(\delta=2\gamma\).

Substituting in \(3\gamma-2\delta=6\), we get \(3\gamma-4\gamma=6\).

Therefore, \(\gamma=-6\).

Hence \(\delta=-12\).

Then \(\alpha=\gamma+3=-3\) and \(\beta=\delta+1=-11\).

Therefore, \(|\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta|=|-3-11-6-12|=32\).

\(4x-5z=10\)

\(5y-x=-20\)

Also, \(\vec a-\vec b+\hat i=2\hat i+3\hat j-2\hat k\).

\(x=5\)

\(z=2\)
